The right stack also supports timely pay runs, benefits, and year end slips like T4 and RL forms without drama. If you’re not ready to open a Canadian entity, see our[Employer of Record in Canada guide](https://www.bolto.com/blog/canada-employer-of-record-guide) .


Facts that matter in Canada


1. Under CRA rules, employers generally deduct and remit income tax, CPP, and EI from each pay.
2. Quebec generally administers QPP and QPIP through Revenu Quebec alongside CRA processes.
3. Employers generally issue T4 slips and file them with the CRA by the last day of February for the prior tax year.
4. A Record of Employment (ROE) is generally required after an interruption of earnings to support EI claims.
5. Most provinces set minimum vacation pay and statutory holiday pay, so payroll should track entitlements with care.

## What Changed in Canadian Payroll for 2026 (and What’s Coming in 2027)


For 2026, the CPP earnings ceiling is $74,600 and the maximum base CPP contribution for employees and employers is generally $4,230.45 each, with second tier CPP2 contributions applying on earnings between $74,600 and $85,000 (CRA, 2026). See[CPP contributions for 2026](https://www.canada.ca/en/services/benefits/publicpensions/cpp/contributions.html) for the current figures. The 2026 EI employee rate is 1.63 percent on maximum insurable earnings of $68,900, so the maximum employee premium works out to $1,123.07, and employers generally pay 1.4 times the employee premium (CRA, 2026). Details are in[EI premium rates and maximums](https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/tax/businesses/topics/payroll/payroll-deductions-contributions/employment-insurance-ei/ei-premium-rates-maximums.html) .


Looking ahead, the Canada Employment Insurance Commission has confirmed 2027 maximum insurable earnings of $70,800 and an employee rate of $1.64 per $100 (ESDC, 2026), as noted in the[2027 maximum insurable earnings notice](https://www.canada.ca/en/employment-social-development/programs/ei/ei-list/ei-employers/premium-reduction-program/2027-maximum-insurable-earnings.html) . These figures tend to shift each year, so you should plan ahead instead of assuming last year’s numbers carry forward. This is general information, not legal advice, and rules vary by situation and change over time, so consult a qualified employment lawyer or accountant for your specific circumstances.


- Confirm your vendor loads the 2027 CPP and EI tables before your first January 2027 pay run
- Check that CPP2 calculations and year end PIER checks run automatically in your system
- Plan your T4 and RL-1 prep for 2026 slips early so filing season does not catch you off guard

### 1. QuickBooks Payroll (Canada) - Best for QuickBooks-centric Canadian SMBs


QuickBooks Payroll (Canada) slots directly into QuickBooks Online so finance teams can go from timesheets to payroll to books without hopping tools. Canadian SMBs and US startups with a Canadian entity lean on it for CRA and Revenu Québec compliance, fast direct deposit, and smooth year-end workflows. The draw is how smoothly it pushes remittances, ROEs, and T-slips through the same interface that already runs your GL.


*Why it stands out: Tight QBO/QuickBooks Time integration and next-day deposits in higher tiers make compliant payroll feel as simple as posting a journal.*


Canada playbook:


- Automates CRA/RQ deductions and remittances, produces PD7A, supports e-payments.
- Prepares T4, T4A, T5018, RL-1 with CRA/RQ XML; distributes slips via Workforce.
- Calculates CPP/QPP, EI, QPIP, QHSF (Quebec Health Services Fund); tracks WSIB/WSBC/CNESST.
- Handles multi-province rates, vacation/stat holidays, WCB tracking.
- CAD direct deposit: two-day in Core; next-day in Premium/Elite; no contractor deposits.
- Creates ROE files for ROE Web; native QBO and QuickBooks Time sync.


**Pricing & who it’s for:** See[QuickBooks Payroll pricing](https://quickbooks.intuit.com/ca/payroll/pricing/) : Core $30 + $5/employee; Premium $55 + $8/employee; Elite $80 + $15/employee (CAD/month, before promotions). Premium/Elite add next-day deposit and QuickBooks Time. Ideal for 1-200+ employees already on QBO, including multi-province and Québec. Requires a Canadian entity; not an EOR.

## Buying Guide: Pro Tips and Pitfalls for Canadian Payroll Vendors


Pro tips


- Ask how the system handles Quebec, QPP and QPIP require separate logic from CPP and EI
- Confirm T4 plus RL workflows if you have staff in Quebec, many tools get one set right and struggle with the other
- Verify ROE timelines and e filing status so you can issue within the required window after an interruption of earnings
- Check province specific rules for stat holidays and vacation pay, look for configuration by province and by employee class
- Map benefits and taxable benefits to the correct T4 boxes before the first pay run


Pitfalls to avoid


- Picking a US only payroll that lacks Canadian remittance and year end support
- Running separate systems for employees and contractors, which creates reconciliation risk
- Underestimating year end prep, PIER reports catch CPP and EI under or over contributions and can trigger costly corrections
- Ignoring data residency and access controls, especially if you serve compliance-heavy industries

### When are T4 slips due


Under CRA rules, employers are generally required to issue and file T4 slips by the last day of February for the previous calendar year. The best payroll software canada automates this process and provides employee self serve access.


### Do I need to issue an ROE for every termination


Under CRA rules, employers are generally required to issue an ROE when there is an interruption of earnings, including terminations, certain leaves, and long unpaid absences. The best payroll software canada should let you create and e-file ROEs directly.


### How do Quebec rules affect my payroll setup


Quebec uses QPP and QPIP managed through Revenu Quebec, plus RL slips at year end. Choose the best payroll software canada that supports dual filing with CRA and Revenu Quebec.
